name: Corporate Creations
old_description: Established in 1995 and based right here in Omaha Nebraska, Corporate Creations specializes in custom screen printing, embroidery and promotional products for the Omaha Metro area including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, LaVista and Papillion.
about:
Corporate Creations was founded in 1995 in Omaha, Nebraska, by Wade Lewis while he was an undergraduate at the University of Nebraska at Omaha. Lewis initially launched Greek Creations to serve fraternity and sorority merchandise needs, and the success of that venture led friends and family to request similar custom screen printing, embroidery, and promotional products for their own organizations. Corporate Creations was born from that demand and remains headquartered at 9001 F Street in Omaha, serving the surrounding metro communities including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, LaVista, and Papillion.

The company provides custom decoration services centered on screen printing and embroidery, supplemented by a promotional product sourcing program that offers access to over 700,000 items. In-house capabilities include graphic design, digitizing for embroidery, art proofing with a 48-hour turnaround, and rush production options. Orders are produced at their Omaha facility with typical lead times of 10 business days after art approval. Minimum order quantities are set at six pieces for embroidery, 12 pieces for screen printing, and 100 pieces for most promotional products, though embroidery reorders carry no minimum.

Corporate Creations serves a broad base of local clients: businesses, clubs, sports teams, churches, charities, schools, universities, and non‑profit organizations throughout the Omaha metro area. The company also continues to support Greek‑life organizations through its affiliated brand Greek Creations. Customers range from small community groups to larger corporate accounts, all receiving the same design‑to‑delivery workflow.

The business was started to simplify and improve the way groups purchased custom merchandise, and that mission persists in a focus on low minimums, transparent pricing, and a collaborative art process that includes two free revisions. The company highlights its award‑winning design team and its recognition as Omaha Magazine’s Best of Omaha Custom T‑Shirt Store winner from 2021 through 2025 as evidence of its service quality.

name: Corporate Woodworking, Inc.
old_description: When your project involves custom architectural woodworking and requires the use of a firm that can deliver and install the highest quality product in the timeframe needed, Corporate Woodworking, Inc. (CWI) is the only choice. As one of the Andersen Companies, along with affiliate Andersen Interior Contracting, CWI operates with the same dedication to customer service and strong relationships that are the hallmark of any Dan Andersen owned business.
about:
Corporate Woodworking, Inc. (CWI) operates from Fairfield, New Jersey, as part of the Andersen Companies group founded by Dan Andersen. Andersen began his career in 1974 working from his basement after experience as an estimator and project manager in New York and New Jersey. He incorporated the Andersen Corporation, grew it significantly, then sold it in 1986 to start Andersen Interior Contracting. In 1989 he launched Corporate Woodworking as a dedicated high‑end architectural woodworking firm, bringing over key staff from his earlier ventures. The business remains privately held under Andersen’s ownership.

CWI specializes in custom architectural millwork, handling engineering, fabrication, and installation of reception areas, wall paneling (including exotic and blueprint‑matched veneers and opaque lacquer finishes), doors and sidelights, and pantry/cafe/servery units. The shop produces thousands of square feet of paneling and thousands of door systems annually, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

The company serves the commercial construction industry, supplying corporate offices, institutional projects, and other interior build‑outs where high‑quality millwork is required. Typical customers include architects, general contractors, and end‑users seeking coordinated fabrication and installation of complex woodwork packages.

CWI differentiates itself through the “Andersen Way” — a philosophy built on relationships, integrity, agility, teamwork, and efficiency — and through its participation in the Architectural Woodwork Institute’s Quality Certification Program (QCP), which validates adherence to stringent design and manufacturing standards.

name: Corteco USA
old_description: Welcome to Corteco, your premier spare parts supplier in the Independent Aftermarket. As a proud member of the global Freudenberg Group, we specialize in delivering components essential for optimal vehicle and machinery performance. With a comprehensive range of over 26,000 products, including sealing solutions, vibration control with rubber-metal parts, and premium cabin air filtration, we ensure OEM quality that exceeds industry standards.
about:
Corteco USA operates from Milan, Ohio, as the North American aftermarket arm of the Freudenberg Group, a global technology company. The business supplies spare parts to independent repair garages and distributors, leveraging the Freudenberg portfolio of original-equipment components.

The company offers a catalog of more than 26,000 products across four main categories: sealing solutions such as oil seals and gaskets (including the Simmerring® brand), rubber-to-metal components for vibration control, steering and suspension parts numbering over 7,000 references, and cabin air filtration with roughly 850 filter variations. The sealing line includes the iconic Simmerring® radial shaft seal, while the rubber-to-metal range covers engine mounts, suspension bushings, and driveline dampers. The steering and suspension assortment encompasses bushings, ball joints, tie rods, and complete kits. Filtration focuses on cabin air filters with activated carbon and particulate media. Customers access the range through an online catalog (ecatcorteco.com) and a dedicated seal-finder tool (findyourseal.com).

Corteco serves the independent automotive aftermarket, targeting passenger cars, heavy-duty trucks, two-wheelers, and emerging e-mobility platforms. Its parts are sold to independent garages and wholesale distributors worldwide.

The brand positions itself on OE-quality standards, emphasizing that its Corteco and TransTec labels deliver original-equipment performance backed by Freudenberg engineering.

name: Country Pure Foods Corporate
old_description: Country Pure Foods is the premier manufacturer of beverages including
about:
Country Pure Foods is headquartered in Akron, Ohio, and traces its origins to 1995 when a private equity firm merged two regional portion‑juice companies, Ohio Pure Foods and Natural Country Farms, to form Country Pure Farms. The business later rebranded as Country Pure Foods and is now partnered with private‑equity firm Blue Point Capital Partners LLC.

The company manufactures portioned and multi‑serve juices, plant‑based beverages, and frozen novelties. Through a series of acquisitions — including Ardmore Farms (1998), Vitality’s portion‑products division (2006), Cal Tex Citrus (2012), Quality Kitchens (2014), Ridgefield’s Brand Corp (2016), and Silver Springs Citrus (2017) — it has built a national production footprint with facilities in multiple states. It operates as a large‑scale co‑packer and private‑label supplier, offering a broad line of beverage products and packaging formats.

Its customers span foodservice (restaurants, healthcare, K‑12 schools), retail, and co‑pack channels. Brands such as Ardmore Farms and SideKicks are sold directly to schools and foodservice distributors, while private‑label products serve retail and foodservice accounts nationwide.

The company states its mission is to “champion success by delivering unparalleled food and beverage solutions.” It emphasizes its position as the largest supplier of portion juice to the foodservice industry, a diverse supplier base, and SQF certification as markers of quality and reliability.

about:
Country Snacks Manufacturing, doing business as Carolina Country Snacks, operates a snack food production facility in Henderson, North Carolina. The company specializes in pork-based snacks cooked daily on site.

The plant produces pork rinds, pork skins, popcorn cracklins, pork rind strips, and fatback skins. Products include Old Time Fatback Skins and sweet and mild BBQ cracklins, all marketed as low-carbohydrate options containing less than 1% carbs. Snacks are packaged in 1.75-ounce bags and sold online in cases of 12 or 24 bags.

The company serves consumers following low-carb diets such as Atkins, as well as home cooks who incorporate pork rinds into recipes. Direct-to-consumer online sales are the primary channel, with no mention of wholesale or foodservice distribution in the available information.

Carolina Country Snacks differentiates itself by cooking pork rinds and skins daily and by offering a crunchy texture alternative to conventional light and puffy rinds. The emphasis on low-carb formulation targets a specific dietary niche.

name: Craftco
old_description: Started as a job shop in 1981 by founders Billy and Marva Craft, Craftco has grown to become a nationwide leader in welding, manufacturing, materials handling, assembly and processing. We operate out of our 25,000-square-foot facility right here in Sheridan, Wyoming, and we take pride in building relationships and solving problems through customer service. Read about our services, capabilities, and even some of the products we build.
about:
Craftco began in 1981 as a one-person welding shop in Sheridan, Wyoming, founded by Billy and Marva Craft. The company remains a family-run business that has expanded from welding into a full-service manufacturing operation.

Today Craftco provides welding and fabrication (including heavy plate forming, waterjet cutting, and certified structural welding), precision CNC machining (turning and milling to tight tolerances), materials processing (raw stock management, precision sawing), coating and assembly (multi-layer protective coatings, sub-assembly, turnkey builds), and engineering and design support (DFM analysis). All services operate under one roof at the 25,000-square-foot facility, serving projects ranging from one-off components to ongoing production partnerships.

The company serves customers nationwide across mining, firearms manufacturing, fossil fuel extraction, robotics, commercial and residential construction, structural building, and oil and gas. A notable international project in 2012 delivered wear liner plates to the Antofagasta mine in Chile. Craftco also partners with large commercial contractors and agricultural equipment builders throughout the Rocky Mountain region and beyond.

Craftco positions itself as more than a job shop, emphasizing engineering-driven problem solving and long-term partnerships. Its stated mission focuses on quality, value, professionalism, integrity, safety, teamwork, and respect, guided by a “Code of the West” ethos. The firm invests in new technology through industry conferences such as FabTech and maintains a fleet of vehicles for on-site service.

name: Creative Composites Group, Augusta Molding Division
old_description: Creative Composites Group can help you advance your infrastructure projects beyond the limitations of traditional materials. We are the largest manufacturer of structural composites in the U.S. with innovative products across multiple industries.
about:
Creative Composites Group’s Augusta Molding Division operates from Augusta, Maine, as part of the Kenway Composites business unit. The division belongs to Creative Composites Group (CCG), a U.S.-based collection of composite manufacturers owned by Hill & Smith Holdings PLC, a UK-listed engineering group with divisions in engineered solutions, roads & security, and galvanizing services. CCG was formed to combine the expertise of several established composite companies, though a specific founding year for the Augusta operation is not publicly stated.

The division produces fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) structural components and systems, offering design-build, structural fabrication, manufacturing, and engineering services. Its capabilities extend to industrial field services, specialized coatings, FRP repair and maintenance, tank and tower installation, lining, and pulp mill repair. The group emphasizes turnkey solutions from concept through installation, leveraging advanced composite manufacturing processes across its network of facilities.

Customers span telecommunications and data centers, energy generation and distribution, marine, rail, housing, pulp and paper, water and wastewater treatment, and chemical storage. The company cites telecom and data centers as a served industry, while its parent group’s portfolio includes infrastructure markets such as energy, marine, and rail.

CCG positions itself as the largest manufacturer of structural composites in the United States, differentiating through vertical integration of design, engineering, and manufacturing across multiple specialized brands. The organization highlights over 60 years of collective field service experience and an integrated model that combines the capabilities of its member companies to deliver corrosion-resistant, lightweight, and long-lasting composite solutions.
